annotations.text: A deep nested-implication shell in the style of Dau's theorem-proving examples. Its point is that it looks deeper than it is: a vacuous double negation sits at the third level, and one DC- takes the shell from four cut levels to three without changing what it says.
One step, and the whole of it: erase a double cut. The graph is logically unchanged and structurally simpler, which is the distinction the exemplar exists to draw.
DC- is meaning-preserving in any context, which is why this is a simplification and not an inference. Nothing is proved here; something is *seen*.
